thread:
robin: FYI raising an escalation from ACME — they started seeing ~10% of responses fail with 'invalid JSON' when using structured output (JSON mode) after yesterday's model roll.
They say retries are causing billing spikes. Customer sent one sanitized sample (see below). Can eng-sre / eng-ml triage?

robin: sample (sanitized):
```
{"user_id": "[REDACTED]", "transactions": [ { "id": "tx_123", "amount": 42.00, }, ], "summary": "approved" }
```

robin: note the trailing comma after 42.00 — customer says they never saw this before the roll. They suspect model variant or redaction interplay.

tonY: can you paste the route + model name + approximate window? Also need the request id(s) and any SDK versions.

robin: route: /v1/generate (structured_output). model: redwood/gpt-07b-quant-v2. Spike started ~2025-03-12T09:15:00Z, persisted ~45m. I pulled logs for one request id: r-01Hk... (sanitized). SDK: node 3.2.1.

tony: ok — first pass: we need server logs (raw response body), tracer span for that request, and whether redaction was active on that customer (redaction_policy=pii). If redaction removed quotes around fields, that could break JSON. Also check if any middleware ran a pretty-printer that inserted trailing commas.

sam: quick mitigation idea: enable structured-output debug for that customer and route sampling to 100% for 2h so we can capture raw model output pre-redaction + post-redaction. Also we can configure a tolerant JSON parser middleware that attempts common fixes (strip trailing commas, convert single quotes) before returning parse failure errors — but only for triage, not as permanent behavior.

eli: adding to that — we don't currently emit a metric that breaks down parse failures by (model, route, redaction_policy). I recommend creating jsonmode.parse_failures{model,route,redaction_policy} and a companion jsonmode.parser_corrections{model,route,correction_type}. That will help surface whether redaction correlates with failures.

robin: customer also mentioned retries from their side. We should capture attempt count and any retry headers to estimate billing impact. Can support ask them for a small sample of failing responses (maybe base64) so we can repro locally?

deploy-bot: canary roll redwood/gpt-07b-quant-v2 v202 -> v203 completed 2025-03-11T22:40:12Z (canary 10%). No automated rollbacks triggered.

tony: timeline plan: I'll grep logs for "invalid JSON" + model name between 09:00-10:30 UTC and collect up to 200 failing raw responses to s3://redwood-triage/acme/jsonmode/1911112222. robin — can you confirm access and collect customer consent for raw samples?

sam: I'll enable per-customer debug sampling and flip on pre-redaction capture for the route. Doing that now as a temporary flag: structured_output.capture_raw=true for customer=acme-payments, TTL=2h. Will post when it's live.

eli: I'll add the two new metrics to the infra-metrics tier and create a dashboard tile: parse failure rate over time, stacked by redaction_policy, plus a table of top 10 offending prompts. Also add an alert (warning at >1% and critical at >5% for 15m).

robin: security note — when we capture raw model output we must not persist sensitive tokens. We should apply redaction only after any tolerant parsing or parser-correction attempts are audited. For triage we need both raw+redacted but store raw transiently and mark for deletion after 7 days.

sam: agreed. I'll ensure captures land encrypted and with auto-delete retention=7d.

eli: one more potential cause — quantization/compilation kernel change could alter tokenization boundaries causing the model to emit a trailing comma token sequence more often. We'll correlate failures with kernel/compilation metadata (serving runtime tags). Add label serving_runtime=kernel_vX to metrics.

robin: action items summary: 
- tony: collect logs + raw responses to s3 by EOD (owner)
- sam: enable debug capture for acme for 2h and ensure retention/encryption (in progress)
- eli: add metrics + dashboard + alerts (ETA 3 hours)
- robin: request customer consent + sample base64 payloads and send via secure share (owner)

robin: if we can reproduce locally I'll try the tolerant-parser approach (attempt fix -> reserialize -> run existing validator). If that reduces failures we can ship a controlled parser-correction path behind a feature flag, plus auditor metrics for every correction.

tony: note for playbook update: add a step that when jsonmode parse failures spike, triage redaction + runtime kernel + recent model roll. Also include a checklist for capturing pre-redaction raw model output.

robin: agreed. I'll update playbook after this incident. I'll ping customer with the brief plan now.

sam: enabled capture; sampling live for acme-payments. Will post sample links here once processed. :thumbsup:

eli: created metric + dashboard draft (link: https://console.redwood/dashboards/draft/jsonmode-1911112222) — tagging you all.

robin: thanks — assigning EOD follow-ups. We'll reconvene if any new spikes occur.

robin: closing loop for now — will reopen thread if we have a reproducible failure or a rollback is needed.
